findings.title: Review dispatch validity omits policy revocation and generation bounds
findings.diagnosis: Reviews remain authorized at and after recorded policy revocation, a new correction generation, and the issuing generation wall-time end. Review records have no explicit lease generation binding. The reservation branch applies policy revocations; the review branch does not.

evidence.observation: Static source inspected before Phase 1 freeze.
Static source inspected before Phase 1 freeze.

Reviews remain authorized at and after recorded policy revocation, a new correction generation, and the issuing generation wall-time end. Review records have no explicit lease generation binding. The reservation branch applies policy revocations; the review branch does not.

fix.action: Bind each new review dispatch to its issuing lease generation (approval sequence and head anchor). Derive its effective end from the minimum of its original TTL, that generation's wall end, applicable core revocations, and dated policy revocations. Treat the unit's correction approval from Independent validation as revoking the old review generation. Refuse authorization when current policy or generation evidence is missing for a contract-bound generation.
fix.why: The review validity branch currently omits policySeen, generation expiry, and own-unit correction generation changes. A shared effective-validity calculation prevents the reservation and review branches from enforcing different revocation rules.

verification.method: Run TestAuditorD4RejectReviewAfterPolicyRevocation with times immediately before, exactly at, and after the event.
verification.expected: Before-event control authorized; tie and later launches unauthorized.
Forward stage progression preserves eligible review launches; correction generation and wall end revoke old review launches.

verification.method: Exercise real host reconcile with stored plans and generation bindings, including reversed revocation ingestion.
verification.expected: Same minimum end and BLOCK findings in all event orders.

fix.tradeoffs: Old packets have no explicit generation identity. A compatibility rule must fail closed when it cannot establish authority. Clamping reviews to the generation wall end may require issuing a new generation before a delayed review. A different review lifetime would require an explicit human-approved contract change, outside D4.
fix.alternative: Infer the immutable generation from the packet's anchored core prefix and retained plan instead of adding a stored field. This reduces schema change but requires equally strict evidence and expiry checks.

findings.title: Restoring the old policy revives launch eligibility in a revoked generation
findings.diagnosis: The real hook first refuses a changed policy and persists policy_revocation. Restoring original policy bytes makes replay return LaunchEligible:true and NextAction:LAUNCH_WORKER for the same old reservation. Replay checks DeriveLease and current policy but ignores historical host policy_revocation.

evidence.observation: Static source inspected before Phase 1 freeze.
Static source inspected before Phase 1 freeze.

The real hook first refuses a changed policy and persists policy_revocation. Restoring original policy bytes makes replay return LaunchEligible:true and NextAction:LAUNCH_WORKER for the same old reservation. Replay checks DeriveLease and current policy but ignores historical host policy_revocation.

fix.action: Make replayResult and fresh reservation issuance consult persisted revocations for the selected generation before setting launch_eligible. Once that generation is revoked, restored policy bytes must not revive it. Require a new approved generation and a new reservation for a new launch.
fix.why: DeriveLease reads core records and the current policy. It cannot see the host's policy_revocation history. The hook must incorporate that history into the same monotone effective end used by reconciliation.

verification.method: Run TestAuditorD4PolicyRestoreDoesNotReviveHook through the real hook request parser.
verification.expected: Changed policy is refused and recorded. Restoring original bytes leaves the old reservation replay ineligible.

verification.method: Add controls for fresh reservation issuance after restoration, a newly approved generation, and a receipt after the revocation tie.
verification.expected: Old generation cannot launch; new approved generation can obtain a distinct reservation; reconciliation agrees with hook eligibility.

fix.tradeoffs: Policy rollbacks will require a new approved generation instead of silently restoring launch authority. Existing historical reservations must remain charged and replayable as ineligible records.
fix.alternative: Record policy revocation in a core event consumed by lease derivation. This makes the authority calculation central but changes the core event contract and requires wider review.

findings.title: Reconciliation authorizes a review receipt from the implementation worker
findings.diagnosis: A real review packet names an independent reviewer. Its receipt instead names the implementation worker/model/provider. review-import rejects the receipt. host reconcile accepts it as Authorized with no Unauthorized entry. The scan drops route identity and packet/target bindings.

A real review packet names an independent reviewer. Its receipt instead names the implementation worker/model/provider. review-import rejects the receipt. host reconcile accepts it as Authorized with no Unauthorized entry. The scan drops route identity and packet/target bindings.

fix.action: Extend scanLedger and LedgerRun to retain launch identity from the receipt. Before classifying a review launch as authorized, compare actual worker, provider, model, effort, packet digest, project root and target bindings with its recorded dispatch. Check the actual route's required independence. Apply equivalent available route bindings to implementation reservations.
fix.why: scanLedger currently discards every receipt field except run_id, mode and started_at. Reconcile can therefore return clean for a launch that review-import already proves belongs to the wrong route.

verification.expected: The wrong actual reviewer route produces UNAUTHORIZED_DISPATCH as BLOCK during reconciliation, even without importing the report.

verification.method: Use independent, correctly bound running and completed reviewer receipts as positive controls; vary worker/model/provider/effort and packet/target independently.
verification.expected: Correct launches remain authorized; mismatches block. Missing or unfinished reports grant no review credit but do not alone make an otherwise legitimate launch unauthorized.

fix.tradeoffs: Ledger fixtures and backward compatibility must handle missing identity fields honestly. Do not require a completed report merely to authorize a launch; report credit remains a separate import decision.
fix.alternative: Extract a launch-binding validator shared by review import and reconciliation, separate from report/state validation. This reduces duplication while preserving in-progress launch reconciliation.
